articles.body:
Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena has caught the eye of Arsenal, while Juventus are weighing up approaches for Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal are keeping tabs on Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena, TEAMtalk reports. An offer worth €80 million is expected to be required to secure the 25-year-old's transfer, as the Gunners explore the market for a top option to play on the left flank. The Premier League side could face competition from Bayern Munich for Baena, who has scored five goals and provided three assists in 11 LaLiga matches this season. Arsenal could raise funds for this with the exit of midfielder Martín Zubimendi, amid interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old has struggled to start regularly since the arrival of Bruno Guimarães and the Gunners would want a fee around the €60 million that they parted with to land him from Real Sociedad in July 2025.

- Juventus are weighing up approaches for Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun, with plans to land a striker in January, Calciomercato reports. The Serie A club are keen to acquire a physical front man in the next transfer window, when they are expected to have around €100 million available to reinforce their squad. Šeško, 23, hasn't featured for United since Sept. 16 in the EFL Cup against Brighton due to injury, while a move for 25-year-old Balogun could be possible after Monaco accepted an initial €40 million offer from Everton in the summer before the deal fell through.

- Manchester United are considering a move for Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney as they prioritize adding depth at the No. 9 position, according to Football Insider. The Red Devils are monitoring the 30-year-old, who has scored 12 goals in nine Saudi Pro League matches this season, with several other options also on their shortlist. Toney has been in Saudi Arabia since joining Al Ahli from Brentford in the summer of 2024.

- Barcelona are interested in Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall, according to Football Insider. Bergvall, 20, chose Spurs over Barcelona in 2024, but the Blaugrana are still monitoring him, though Spurs are in control of his future as his contract is not set to expire until the summer of 2031. The Sweden international has made four Premier League appearances this season and has also emerged on the radar of Napoli.

- Al-Hilal have ended their pursuit of Manchester United midfielder Bruno Fernandes, TalkSPORT reports. The Saudi Pro League club were strongly linked with a move for the 32-year-old over the summer, but they aren't expected to make a new approach for him in January, with no plans to free up any of their overseas player slots. articles.headline: Romeo Lavia: Meeting Eden Hazard gave me extra motivation to succeed at Chelsea
articles.description: Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia has said a meeting with fellow Belgian Eden Hazard has provided extra motivation as he looks to build on an encouraging start to the season.
articles.headlineJa: ロメオ・ラビア：エデン・アザールとの面会がチェルシーでの成功へのさらなるモチベーションになった
articles.descriptionJa: チェルシーのミッドフィールダー、ロメオ・ラビアは、同じベルギー代表のエデン・アザールとの面会が、好調なシーズン開幕を足掛かりにさらなる活躍を目指す中、さらなるモチベーションになったと語った。
articles.body:
Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia has said a meeting with fellow Belgian Eden Hazard has provided extra motivation as he looks to build on an encouraging start to the season.

Blues great Hazard returned to Stamford Bridge for Saturday's 2-0 Premier League victory over Manchester United and greeted players following the final whistle.

The 35-year-old won six major honours, including two Premier League titles, with Chelsea and scored 110 goals in 352 appearances for the club before moving to Real Madrid in 2019.

Lavia said seeing his compatriot after the weekend win provided an additional incentive to continue improving.

"He's a very important figure for me," Lavia said on Chelsea's website.

"We speak quite a lot. It was good to see him out here and I could see in his eyes he was happy for me and proud. It gives me that extra motivation."

Lavia has been hampered by persistent injury problems since joining Chelsea from Southampton for an initial £53 million ($71.4m) fee in 2023.

However, he has been included in the Blues' matchday squad for every Premier League fixture so far this season and was recently recalled to the Belgium squad.

The 22-year-old has now completed 90 minutes in consecutive appearances, against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup and United in the league.

"As long as I feel good, I will do everything possible to help the team get results," Lavia said.

"I'm feeling good, so I am very happy with my performance.

- Cole Palmer should have been sent off for Mateus Fernandes clash - KMI panel

- Xabi Alonso: Romeo Lavia 'in top form' after Chelsea beat Man United

"I'm still young and there are a lot of areas I can improve. We try to tick them off during the week. It's a process.

"All I can say is the work we are doing with all the people at the club is going well so far. It's just about keeping it going and hopefully we can continue this way."

Chelsea sit fourth in the Premier League table with 16 points from nine games since the summer appointment of manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues travel to bottom club Sunderland on Sunday before hosting Leeds following the international break.

articles.headline: NFL Week 9 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips and trade deadline news
articles.description: What now for the Ravens without Lamar Jackson? What are people around the NFL saying about Justin Herbert's struggles? And what's the latest on the looming trade deadline?
articles.headlineJa: NFL第9週の最新情報、噂や疑問、ファンタジー・チップス、トレード期限のニュース
articles.descriptionJa: ラマー・ジャクソンを欠くレイブンズはどうなるのか？ジャスティン・ハーバートの不振についてNFL関係者は何を語っているのか？そして、目前に迫ったトレード期限の最新状況は？
articles.body:
It's Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season, which means two things. First, we're about to hit midseason. Second, the trade deadline is right around the corner. And insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

The Ravens are in a tough spot, dropping to 4-4 and losing not only QB1 Lamar Jackson but also QB2 Tyler Huntley to injuries. What's next for Baltimore? Will the Ravens focus their attention on 2027 or still try to turn things around this season in a tight AFC North? Out west, what's going on with Justin Herbert? The Chargers obviously have big problems at 0-7, and Herbert hasn't played well. What are we hearing on his struggles?

And what about trade buzz? What's the latest around the league? Which teams could be active, and which players could be on the move before the Tuesday deadline? It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 9.

Jump to:

Next steps for the Ravens

Buzz on Herbert's struggles

Deadline intel | Fantasy advice

More notes and nuggets

What's your sense on where the Ravens go from here?

Graziano: Baltimore isn't a throw-in-the-towel type of organization. My sense is that the Ravens will work to solve the problem and will be open to a number of ideas at quarterback with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) out. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano has been announced as their starter for Thursday night against Jacksonville, but if, for example, the Cardinals are done with Jacoby Brissett, Baltimore would be a team I'd expect to at least look into bringing in Brissett for Week 10 on.

Fowler: In the short term, there are several players with lower-cost contracts if the Ravens choose to pursue them. Brissett was with Ravens quarterbacks coach Isaiah Woolfork last season in Arizona. Bears backup Tyson Bagent has familiarity with Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. And some conversations I had early this week made me think the Colts' Daniel Jones is at least on the radar. Baltimore could essentially sign him without spending a lot because of his struggles. Jones' $5.5 million base salary is tradable, and his 2027 guarantees don't trigger until the offseason. He's roughly 11 months post-Achilles tear, so perhaps his play improves.

Graziano: My bigger question is a long-term one involving Jackson's future with the franchise. I believed going into this season that the most important big-picture goal the Ravens had was to get to next offseason with Jackson feeling good about signing an extension that keeps him in Baltimore for years to come. Now that it is apparent that the season isn't going the way he or they hoped, my focus is trying to figure out what comes next for the Ravens and Jackson.

articles.headline: Two-goal hero Matheus Cunha hopes Roma win is turning point for Man United
articles.description: Manchester United's Matheus Cunha said he thinks Tuesday's Champions League comeback win over AS Roma will mark a turning point for his struggling side.
articles.headlineJa: 2ゴールを挙げたヒーロー、マテウス・クーニャはローマ戦の勝利がマン・Uの転換点になることを期待
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのマテウス・クーニャは、火曜日に行われたチャンピオンズリーグのASローマ戦での逆転勝利は、苦境にあるチームにとって転換点になると考えていると語った。
articles.body:
Manchester United's Matheus Cunha said he thinks Tuesday's Champions League comeback win over AS Roma will mark a turning point for his struggling side.

United were 2-0 down at halftime at Old Trafford but struck three goals after the restart, including two from Cunha, to triumph, 3-2.

"I think it's a real dream to be here," Cunha told TNT Sports after the game.

"We always dream of being here, of being part of something very big, and to have this comeback in a Champions League game like this, at a time when we weren't doing well, I think it really shows the character of our team."

Cunha went into the game feeling pressure after having not scored since Sept. 20.

"If I have to be part of a difficult moment, that's ok, because I think there comes a time when you have to embrace responsibility, with privilege, and step up during a difficult time," he said.

"Responsibility is a delight...it makes me happy to live up to it. I'm very happy to be a part of this, to be winning again after a while without winning here.

"It shows what Manchester United is like, it shows what kind of players are here, that even in a difficult moment they can decide the game."

Cunha, who joined the Red Devils in 2025 from Wolves, said Tuesday's game was a day he will remember fondly even though he was sent off late in the encounter.

He celebrated his second goal by jumping into the supporters and being yellow-carded by the referee.

Cunha then received a second yellow in stoppage time for a foul.

He will avoid UEFA punishment for failing to go straight to the dressing room following his dismissal. 

A spokesperson for the governing body said: "The UEFA official reports did not mention anything about this incident.

"Therefore the automatic one-match ban following two yellow cards should not be extended for this reason. We are not investigating further this matter."

Cunha became the first player in Champions League history to win a penalty, score a goal and be sent off in the same match.

"I think it was my most beautiful day at this stadium," the Brazilian forward said. "I think a game like this is a moment to change everything ... the kind of atmosphere we always hope to create here. We're ready for it."

Tuesday's victory halted a four-match losing streak as well as a nine-game run without a win for United and it also eased the pressure on coach Michael Carrick.

Asked if this was a pivotal moment in their season, Cunha said: "If not now, when? I hope it's now. I'm very happy. I think my teammates are very happy.

"It's good that we are working so hard and facing so much criticism to get through this moment together. I think everybody came back with such a mindset in the second half and we did what we had to do. I hope it will be a turning point this season."

Cunha believes his team can work on "a new Manchester United," that is not constantly reminded about past glories.

articles.headline: Browns QB Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol; status vs. Saints unclear
articles.description: The Browns have placed starting QB Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol, the team announced Wednesday, leaving his status for Sunday's matchup against the Saints in question.
articles.headlineJa: ブラウンズのQBデショーン・ワトソンが脳震盪プロトコル入り、セインツ戦の出場は不透明
articles.descriptionJa: ブラウンズは水曜日、先発QBのデショーン・ワトソンを脳震盪プロトコルに移行させたと発表した。これにより、日曜日のセインツ戦への出場可否は不透明となっている。
articles.body:
BEREA, Ohio -- The Cleveland Browns announced on Wednesday that starting quarterback Deshaun Watson has been placed in the NFL's concussion protocol, putting his availability for Sunday's road game against the New Orleans Saints in question.

In a statement, the Browns said that Watson reported to the team's medical staff Tuesday morning that he was experiencing concussion symptoms.

Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker on the opening possession of last Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers and missed three plays while he was checked for a concussion. Cleveland said he was administered a game-day concussion evaluation by an unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant and cleared to the return to play. Watson was then evaluated by the medical staff postgame and again on Monday and did not show any symptoms before reporting them on Tuesday morning.

The Browns are 5-3 and in third place in the AFC North but are one game behind the first-place Steelers. Watson has started the first eight games of the season, completing 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions.

If Watson cannot clear the concussion protocol in time to play against the Saints, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to make his first start of the season. A 2025 fifth-round pick, Sanders started seven games as a rookie but has served as the backup this season after losing a quarterback competition to Watson. Sanders has thrown just three passes this season.

Dillon Gabriel returned from injured reserve last week and served as the emergency QB in Week 8. Rookie Taylen Green is also on the roster.

articles.headline: Tennis great Rafa Nadal accepts Real Madrid offer to join board of directors
articles.description: Tennis legend Rafa Nadal confirmed on Wednesday he has accepted an offer to become a member of Real Madrid's board of directors.
articles.body:
Tennis legend Rafa Nadal confirmed on Wednesday he has accepted an offer to become a member of Real Madrid's board of directors.

Nadal, a long-time fan of the team, has been an honorary member of Real Madrid since March 2017.

"For Real Madrid and for all madridistas, it is an immense honor that a figure of his sporting and human stature, a reference in Spanish and global sports, joins our Board of Directors and contributes, from this role, to the present and future of our club," a club statement said of Nadal on Wednesday.

Nadal, 40, posted on Instagram a photograph of himself when he was a toddler wearing the Madrid kit, and wrote: "I would like to thank President Florentino Pérez and the Board for inviting me to join the Board of Directors of @realmadrid. I have accepted this invitation with great enthusiasm, keen to learn and contribute as much as I can."

Nadal retired from tennis in 2024 having won 22 major titles -- including a record 14 French Opens -- as well as 36 Masters titles and two Olympic gold medals.

Madrid added: "Nadal has had a legendary sports career.

"However, his persona represents much more than his achievements: his talent, his continuous drive for improvement, his capacity for sacrifice, his competitiveness, his humility, his respect for rivals and teammates, and his solidarity make him an example both on and off the court.

"All these values are part of Real Madrid's identity, and Rafael Nadal has represented and upheld them throughout his sporting life, becoming a role model for millions of people around the world."

Madrid's General Assembly on Nov. 21 will have to ratify Nadal's appointment as a new member of the board.

articles.headline: NBA Power Rankings: Summing up all 30 teams' starts
articles.description: Here's where all 30 NBA teams rank after two weeks of action, plus the four words used to describe how each team has started the season.
articles.body:
Just two weeks into the NBA season, storylines have been flipped as injuries and surprise surges reverberate around the league. 

The Philadelphia 76ers have dominated their opponents early -- and are having some fun in the process. Meanwhile, the reigning champion New York Knicks are attempting to claw themselves back into the top echelon after starting the season 0-3. 

It's in the West where things have started to heat up. The Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves are dealing with injuries to their stars, making way for players such as the Memphis Grizzlies' Ty Jerome to have an early impact in his team's standings. The Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Doncic is making an early MVP case and doesn't seem to be slowing down after scoring 42 and 45 points in his past two games. And the Portland Trail Blazers, sans Ja Morant as he deals with an injury, are showing that depth is what will set teams apart across the league.

In our second iteration of Power Rankings since the season started, our NBA insiders assigned four words to describe each team's start to 2026-27, and break down why things are -- or are not -- working. 

Note: Team rankings are based on where members of our panel (ESPN's Jamal Collier, Michael C. Wright, Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Ben Golliver, Kris Rhim and Anthony Slater) think teams belong.

2026-27 record: 7-1

The Rockets navigated the choppy waters of Kevin Durant's first season nearly rudderless without floor general Fred VanVleet, who sustained a season-ending knee injury before the start of training camp. articles.headline: Man United fans throwing tennis balls is part of soccer's rich history of supporter protests
articles.description: After Manchester United's match was disrupted by tennis balls thrown onto the pitch, here are some of the various ways fans have made themselves heard.
articles.body:
It looked like Manchester United's woeful run was primed to continue on Tuesday as Michael Carrick's faltering side fell 2-0 down inside the first 20 minutes of their UEFA Champions League tie against AS Roma, much to the audible dismay of the Old Trafford crowd.

With the home team offering little in the way of attacking impetus and repeated defensive errors leaving the back line vulnerable, the atmosphere inside the stadium was largely despondent. Indeed, with their team already two goals behind, disgruntled fans took it upon themselves to stage a planned protest in the first half as dozens of tennis balls were hurled from the stands onto the pitch to disrupt the game.

Play was halted for several minutes while the balls were cleared, allowing United to limp onto the halftime break. The interval then seemed to ignite a fire under Carrick's beleaguered side, who staged an exhilarating second-half comeback to win  3-2.

While it's unlikely the tennis ball protest made as much impact on proceedings as the halftime barracking delivered by Carrick and his staff, it certainly raised awareness of the discontent mounting among the supporter base.

While chants and banners in the terraces are a fairly commonplace way for soccer fans to voice their discontent, sometimes they step it up a notch. Here's a look at some of the various approaches adopted by supporters to really get the message across.

- As fan protests continue, did United's comeback save Carrick?

- Why Man United are so bad at hiring managers post-Ferguson

- Milner completes NYC Marathon in just over three hours

Foreign objects

United's tennis ball protest during the Roma game certainly wasn't the first of its kind, with Celtic supporters orchestrating a much more effective demonstration last year by hurling balls onto the pitch during a Europa League game against Stuttgart.

Borussia Dortmund's famous "Yellow Wall" also brought a 2024 Bundesliga match against SC Freiburg to a halt by throwing balls and chocolate coins onto the pitch in protest of an unpopular media investment proposal being floated by the German football association.

Perhaps the most unusual pitch pelting on record came during the 2016 League One game between Charlton Athletic and Coventry City in 2016 when both sets of fans decided to protest against their respective owners by lobbing hundreds of little pink, plastic pigs out onto the turf.

Plane banners

A tried-and-true method of getting your message seen, several fan groups have organized banners to be flown over their stadiums on match day in order to broadcast their grievances to the wider world. Indeed, Manchester United fans have rallied against their owners in the skies above Old Trafford in the past -- notably after reaching the end of their tether with David Moyes' managerial tenure.

articles.headline: 'I'm not Mohamed Salah' - Bradley Barcola doesn't feel Liverpool pressure
articles.description: Liverpool forward Bradley Barcola has insisted that he isn't feeling any pressure following his big-money move from Paris Saint-Germain and won't dwell on the impact of predecessor Mohamed Salah.
articles.body:
Liverpool forward Bradley Barcola has insisted that he isn't feeling any pressure following his big-money move from Paris Saint-Germain and won't dwell on the impact of predecessor Mohamed Salah.

In an interview with Sky Sports, Barcola said that this past summer was the "right time" to leave two-time European champions and that he has always wanted to play in the Premier League.

The France winger, 24, joined the Reds in August in a deal that could be worth up to £123 million ($165m.) He spent three years at PSG after coming up through Lyon's youth ranks.

Barcola has had a mixed start to life on Merseyside so far. He scored a hat trick in Liverpool's Champions League match against LASK but he is yet to score in the Premier League -- although he has bagged himself two assists so far in the league.

His eye-watering price tag means that there are some big expectations attached to him.

When asked about his significant transfer fee, and the long shadow that Salah casts following his move to Trabonszpor, Barcola said: "Firstly, I wasn't the one who decided the transfer fee. So that's not been my problem.

"And regarding Mo Salah, he's a legend here. A huge one. He's done big things here and for that I have an enormous respect for him. But it's not pressure for me at all.

"I'm not Mohamed Salah, so I'm going to try to contribute whatever I can to the club and make my own mark on its history. I don't feel any pressure about that."

The Frenchman also opened up about his decision to leave PSG -- arguably the best club in Europe as it stands.

"Ever since I was young, I've always had the ambition of playing in the Premier League," Barcola added. "For me, it was the right time to leave PSG. I spent so many great years there and won an enormous amount of trophies but it was the right time.

"When a club like Liverpool comes calling, it's a great thing and so I didn't have any doubts. I just knew I had to come here. I'm happy."

- Fenerbahce coach Dirk Kuyt ready for 'very special' reunion with Liverpool

- Liverpool's $500m forward line is failing. Can they turn it around?

Asked if it was difficult to bid farewell to PSG, Barcola said: "Over there, it was a real family. We'd built something very special together [...] But, ultimately, that's just how football is."

Barcola was asked about whether he feels he has his shown his best at Liverpool yet and said that he thinks there is much more to come.

"No, I don't think I'm at my best yet. You still haven't seen the best version of me. We're working with my teammates so they can make the most of my strengths. I think once we really develop that understanding, things will get much better," he said.

Liverpool endured a disappointing 1-0 loss to Arsenal last time out in the Premier League.

They face Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday night before heading to Selhurst Park to take on Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday

articles.headline: Dumonts take over as controlling owners of Mavericks
articles.description: Sivan and Patrick Dumont purchased Miriam Adelson's shares of the Mavericks last month, making the Dumont family the controlling owners of the franchise.
articles.headlineJa: デュモン家がマベリックスの筆頭オーナーに就任
articles.descriptionJa: シヴァンとパトリック・デュモンが先月、ミリアム・アデルソンのマベリックス株式を取得し、デュモン家が同球団の支配権を持つオーナーとなった。
articles.body:
Sivan and Patrick Dumont purchased Miriam Adelson's shares of the Dallas Mavericks last month, making the Dumont family the controlling owners of the franchise with a 69% share.
Adelson has had minimal involvement with the Mavericks since she bought the majority share of the franchise from Mark Cuban in December 2023 along with her daughter and son-in-law. Patrick Dumont has served as the Mavericks' governor since the families took control of the franchise.

"It's really about long-term investment in the city of Dallas," Dumont told ESPN on Tuesday. "The Dumont family is really committed to building what we hope is the best arena in the NBA, a really significant investment in the city that will help create the new 40-year home for the Dallas Mavericks, a great experience for our fans and inspire our team to win championships. That's really what we're focused on. We had the opportunity, and we're really excited about it."

Cuban, who has expressed regret about selling the Mavericks to Adelson and the Dumonts due to being frozen out of the franchise's basketball and business operations, maintains a 27% share of the franchise. According to the terms of the 2023 sale, Dumont can purchase another 20% share from Cuban at the original $3.5 billion valuation.

"Our plan is to look at that and to do that over time," Dumont said. "I just have to tell you: I love Mark. He's been a great family friend for a really long time. He's just a super passionate Mavs fan and he's frustrated. I respect it. We're going to hopefully do him proud. That's my goal -- to make all of our Mavs fans super proud about the success of the team and win a championship."

Dumont, the Las Vegas Sands Co. CEO, has overseen a major overhaul of the franchise during his turbulent tenure as the Mavericks governor.

Dumont drew intense wrath from the fanbase for approving former general manager Nico Harrison's decision to trade perennial MVP candidate Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers months after the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals. Dumont has since taken drastic measures to attempt to position the franchise for success as it pivots to build around Cooper Flagg, the reigning Rookie of the Year who Dallas drafted with the No. 1 overall pick after a historic stroke of lottery luck.

"The most important thing every day is just trying to work harder to get better," Dumont said. "It's something that really applies in life, but it's something that really applies to here. It's been an experience as a new owner in the league. Dallas is a great sports city. I think we have the best fans in the NBA, very passionate, and it's my job to make sure that we win and that we support our fans. I'm really focused on that. I've learned that there are a lot of things you can do -- sometimes they work, sometimes they don't -- but you've got to keep pushing, got to keep going."

articles.headline: Lakers' Luka Doncic has 2nd tech of season rescinded by NBA
articles.description: The technical foul assessed to Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic late in the second quarter of Monday's 138-117 win over the Miami Heat was rescinded, the NBA announced.
articles.headlineJa: NBA、レイカーズのルカ・ドンチッチに科した今季2枚目のテクニカルファウルを取り消し
articles.descriptionJa: NBAは、月曜日のマイアミ・ヒート戦（138-117で勝利）の第2クォーター終盤にロサンゼルス・レイカーズのスター、ルカ・ドンチッチに科されたテクニカルファウルを取り消したと発表した。
articles.body:
The technical foul assessed to Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic late in the second quarter of Monday's 138-117 win over the Miami Heat was rescinded, the NBA announced.

The league's decision reduced Doncic's season total from two technical fouls to one.

After not being a whistled for a tech in his first four games, Doncic's tech Monday had been his second in his past three games before the league's ruling.

"This season," Doncic said on Oct. 21, "I'm trying to not get techs."

A player receives an automatic one-game suspension and a $5,000 fine if whistled for 16 technical fouls during the regular season.

Doncic has reached that number in four of his eight seasons in the league, including last season with the Lakers when he had to serve a one-game suspension during L.A.'s 120-101 victory over the Washington Wizards on March 30.

articles.headline: Raptors' Kawhi Leonard completes knee treatment, begins 'return to play process'
articles.description: Kawhi Leonard has completed a treatment to address left knee swelling and is beginning the "return to play process" in Toronto, the Raptors announced.
articles.headlineJa: ラプターズのカワイ・レナード、膝の治療を完了し「復帰プロセス」を開始
articles.descriptionJa: ラプターズの発表によると、カワイ・レナードは左膝の腫れの治療を完了し、トロントで「復帰プロセス」を開始している。
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard has completed a treatment to address left knee swelling and is beginning the "return to play process" in Toronto, the Raptors announced Tuesday.

The team said it will issue another update in one week. 

Leonard, 35, was sidelined because of left knee swelling after appearing in just two regular-season games for Toronto. An MRI on the knee last month showed no structural damage.

Leonard has previously had issues with his right knee, having multiple surgeries for his meniscus and ACL. 

In two games this season, Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals. He's in his first year back with the Raptors after being traded to Toronto from the LA Clippers this offseason after a scandal-marred conclusion to his six seasons there. He agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the Raptors after the trade.

Leonard previously played one season in Toronto, leading the Raptors to their only NBA championship in 2019 before leaving for the Clippers in free agency.
